As a Staff Software Engineer on the Traffic Team, you will work closely with a distributed, diverse, and passionate team of engineers to improve and maintain part of the platform that millions of developers worldwide rely on in their software development cycle.

The Traffic Team is highly distributed, and you will thrive in an environment of remote work and asynchronous communication. You're expected to have strong written communication skills and be able to develop working relationships with coworkers in locations around the globe. As an engineer at GitHub, you'll always be challenged to solve interesting and novel problems that have a real impact on how the world builds software.

  • Lead technical decision making and architecture

  • Design and implement scalable, reliable and performant solutions for complex problems like rate-limiting, routing, etc.

  • Maintain and improve the GitHub Load Balancer, and other systems related to traffic management at GitHub

  • Write, review, and maintain code primary in Go and Ruby & Rails

  • Mentor other engineers in their technical and architectural decision making

  • Participate in the on-call rotation, and team meetings

    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years building and supporting large, high traffic applications at scale within platform/infrastructure domains
  • 4+ years supporting and building cloud native workloads in Azure, AWS or Google Cloud
  • 2+ years experience maintaining a Load Balancer with proven experience in abuse protection mechanisms for DDoS attacks, load shedding, etc.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills

The Director of Software Engineering is a strategic leadership role responsible for overseeing the end-to-end software development lifecycle, including design, development, implementation, and sustainment. This position demands a deep understanding of both traditional application development and modern DevOps practices to ensure seamless integration, continuous delivery, and operational excellence. The Director will lead a team of skilled managers, developers, analysts, and DevOps professionals, driving innovation and efficiency through the adoption of best practices and technologies.

As SNC's corporate team, we provide the company and its business areas with strategic direction and business support spanning executive management, finance and accounting, operations, human resources, legal, IT, information security, facilities, marketing, and communications.

Responsibilities

The Director of Software Engineering is responsible for defining and communicating the long-term vision and roadmap for software development and DevOps practices while driving organizational transformation toward Agile, CI/CD, and DevOps maturity. This role ensures alignment of technology initiatives with business objectives, champions innovation through technologies such as Infrastructure as Code and AI/ML, and oversees the end-to-end software development lifecycle to guarantee quality, scalability, and security. The Director establishes and enforces best practices for coding standards, secure development (DevSecOps), and compliance frameworks, while implementing and optimizing CI/CD pipelines and containerization across robust cloud environments. The Director also ensures adherence to security and regulatory requirements, proactively manages risks related to software delivery and infrastructure, and maintains operational resilience across platforms.

Qualifications You Must Have

  • Bachelor’s Degree, Information Systems, Business, Computer Science, or related field of study
  • 14+ years of experience in Software Development and/or DevOps, or related position.
  • Higher level relevant degree may substitute for experience.
  • Progressive experience leading technical teams

  • Deep knowledge of cloud architecture (AWS, Azure, GCP).

  • Proven leadership abilities inclusive of successful change management, mentoring, career development, training, succession planning, holding people accountable, and conducting yearly reviews
  • Mastery of the ability to drive innovative thinking, lead and inspire your team, instill collaboration, challenge status quo, manage complex situations, delegate authority, and demonstrate ability to adapt to dynamic situations
  • Proven experience and skills in team building, time management, conflict resolution, communication, briefing, presentation, and strategic thinking
  • Strong communication skills, including the ability to clearly express technical concepts in verbal and written forms; ability to interpret technical requirements
  • Ability to navigate change and uncertainty, make defensible decisions in ambiguity and own those decisions

Qualifications We Prefer

  • Expertise in building high-performing, cross-functional teams.
  • Driving organizational transformation toward agile and DevOps maturity.
  • Familiarity with AI/ML integration in DevOps, Infrastructure as Code, and observability tools.
  • Experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and microservices.
  • Understanding of secure coding practices, DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001).
  • Familiarity with government security requirements.
  • Ability to leverage data-driven decision-making and metrics for DevOps performance (DORA metrics, CI/CD KPIs).
  • Demonstrated passion for ideation, intellectual curiosity, and innovation
  • Experience motivating others to act by creating a shared sense of vision or purpose
  • Proven long-term and strategic perspective that extends beyond the immediate initiatives; visualizes and articulates a clear direction
  • Background in the Aerospace and Defense Industry, the US Department of Defense (Civilian), NASA/Civil or commercial space and/or US Military, with an understanding of defense, aerospace, intelligence, and adjacent markets

Essential Functions

  • Frequent communication with team members and stakeholders.
  • Ability to work in an office or hybrid environment.

  • Must be able to lift up to 10 lbs occasionally.
  • Ability to lead and inspire teams in a highly regulated environment.
  • Ability to manage ambiguity and demonstrate resilience and change agility.
  • Utilize advanced analytical skills to interpret complex data sets, providing actionable insights to support decision-making processes.
  • Foster strong collaboration with other departments, including IT, compliance, and operations, to ensure seamless data flow and usage across the organization.

title: Founder-in-Residence, AI Native Ventures (LG NOVA)
description:
Step into the innovative world of LG Electronics. As a global leader in technology, LG Electronics is dedicated to creating innovative solutions for a better life. Our brand promise, 'Life's Good', embodies our commitment to ensuring a happier life for all. We have a rich history spanning over six decades and a global presence in over 290 locations. Our diverse portfolio includes Home Appliance Solutions, Media Entertainment Solutions, Vehicle Solutions, and Eco Solutions. Our management philosophy, "Jeong-do Management," embodies our commitment to high ethical standards and transparent operations. Grounded in the principles of 'Customer-Value Creation' and 'People-Oriented Management', these values shape our corporate culture, fostering creativity, diversity, and integrity. At LG, we believe in the power of collective wisdom through an inclusive work environment. Join us and become a part of a company that is shaping the future of technology. At LG, we strive to make Life Good for Everyone.

LG NOVA, LG Electronics North America Innovation Center
You are not applying for a job. You are here to found LG's next company.

LG NOVA builds new ventures and spins them out as real businesses. We are looking for a small group of founders to validate and launch the next one, with LG's balance sheet, distribution, and government relationships behind them.


We are currently recruiting for our next Founder in Residence cohort, with the first 90-day validation sprint targeted to begin on October 1, 2027.

This is a founding seat, not an advisory one. If the venture proves out, you lead it as Founder and CEO.

The mandate is open on purpose

We are not handing you a problem to solve. The strongest ventures come from founders who already see something the market has missed, so we are domain agnostic by design. While we are domain agnostic, we are focused on AI-enabled software ventures with strong commercial potential

Bring the problem you have unfair insight into, the buyers you already know, and the conviction that it should exist as a company. Every venture in this cohort is AI-native.

NOTE: We are building software solutions only, so no hardware, no robotics, and nothing capital intensive upfront. Every venture in this cohort is AI-native. The industry is yours to pick. For this cohort we are not considering health or clean tech (other verticals at LG NOVA), so if that is your space, this is not the cohort for it.


Who we are looking for
You are a domain operator with deep access to the buyers in your space. You have built or commercialized something real and have experience raising funding rounds. People in your industry take your call. Maybe you founded before, maybe you raised before, maybe you ran a business line that behaved like a startup. You move fast when the path is unclear, and you close.


The profile we want
Founder, repeat founder, or founding executive experience
Deep expertise and credibility in a specific industry or problem space
A live network of buyers and decision makers in your domain that you can leverage.
A track record of building, commercializing, or scaling something new
Comfort in ambiguity with a bias toward evidence and revenue
A clear view on why AI makes your venture buildable now and not three years ago

What LG NOVA offers
You get resources most early founders would fight for.
A concept testing budget so you can put real money behind proving demand
A de-risking idea to commercialization budget up to 500K, setting you up for Seed round.
Government partnerships in multiple U.S. States that open real doors to pilots, design partners, and first customers
An LG backed fund that gives validated ventures a direct path to capital, so you are not starting your raise from zero
Market research, market sizing, and financial modeling done alongside you, not billed back to you
Engineering services to help you test and build
A competitive stipend at market rates while you do the work
Equity in the venture you just validated and commercialized if it progresses to the Seed round
You validate. We resource it.

How the program runs
The program runs in two sprints.

Sprint 1 is 90 days of validation. You define a specific high value problem, identify the economic buyer, test willingness to pay, and generate hard evidence that a venture should exist. The point is proof, not a product.

Sprint 2 is 180+ days of building toward venture formation. You move from evidence to commercialization, early customers, and the foundation of a company.
If the venture earns it, you become Founder and CEO of a new business built with LG behind you.

What you will do
Develop and sharpen a venture thesis
Run buyer discovery with the people who actually hold the budget
Pin down the economic buyer, the budget owner, and how they buy
Validate the pain, the workflow, and the real size of the demand
Design and test a paid pilot, a design partner program, or an early offering
Secure concrete evidence of willingness to pay, whether a paid pilot, a signed letter of intent with commercial terms, or a design partner agreement, from a named buyer
Build the commercialization plan and the business model
Bring back a recommendation grounded in what the market told you
What success looks like by the end
A clearly defined venture opportunity
A validated customer and economic buyer
Hard evidence of demand
A credible path to revenue
Signed design partners, pilots, or customer commitments
A commercialization plan that scales
Enough conviction that LG should invest and build

The Details
This is a hybrid role based in Santa Clara, California.
The Founder in Residence program is designed as two consecutive 90-day sprints. Compensation is annualized and paid during each sprint as follows:
- Sprint 1 (90 days): Annualized compensation equivalent of $180,000–$200,000, plus a dedicated concept testing budget.
- Sprint 2 (90 days): Annualized compensation equivalent of $200,000–$240,000, contingent upon successful completion of Sprint 1 and selection to continue into the commercialization phase.

We are selecting a very small, highly selective founding cohort for this round, so the bar is high and the opportunity is significant.
If your venture is successfully spun out and you transition into the role of Founder & CEO, your executive compensation package—including salary, equity, and other compensation elements—will be negotiated separately as part of the new company's formation and financing.

How to apply
Send us

- Your resume
- A short founder summary, about one page, answering the three questions below in a few sentences each:
1) What experience have you had building? Pick one venture, product, or business you personally helped build or commercialize. What was the problem, what did you own, and what were the measurable results such as revenue, customers, funding, or adoption?

2) What traction did you have? Tell us about a time you found a real customer need, proved demand, and won early customers. What did you do, and what happened?

3) How do you move? Give us one example of using your network to accelerate something, a key hire, a partnership, a customer relationship, or an industry connection that changed the outcome.

And we give patrons millions of opportunities to enjoy one of life’s greatest satisfactions: the discovery of a good book.

Now’s your chance to join the best team in Brooklyn!

Outreach Ambassador (PT)

Brooklyn Public Library (BPL) is seeking an enthusiastic candidate to fill the role of Outreach Ambassador. The candidate must have excellent outreach, organizational, and communication skills and be comfortable engaging with individuals and groups of all abilities and from a wide range of backgrounds.

Outreach Ambassadors will provide information about community resources to people who attend library programs. Ambassadors will provide referral and support in particular to immigrant communities and participants in BPL English Language Learning programs. Referrals will be made in-person and via telephone, email and text. Outreach Ambassadors will provide administrative support for BPL community outreach initiatives and collect data about the number and types of referrals given.

The Outreach Ambassador must be prepared to travel across the borough to build awareness of the Library’s programs and services. This is a hands-on, active role that requires in-person communication and engagement at a wide range of indoor and outdoor environments including public libraries, city shelters and other housing facilities, and community events.

This is a grant funded position that begins July 1, 2026 and ends June 30, 2027. This position reports to the Immigrant Services Coordinator in the Outreach Department.

  • Conduct outreach at a wide range of year-round community events in Brooklyn.
  • Undertake a range of outreach activities at BPL library locations, community organizations, and in public settings (both indoors and outdoors).
  • Assist with maintaining a list of community programs and services including those local to neighborhoods served.
  • Actively refer Library patrons to relevant Library programs, community organizations, and service providers.
  • Plan, set-up equipment, and attend scheduled outreach events.
  • Plan, promote, and present at information sessions both in person and virtually.
  • Provide clear information about BPL services and programs at in-person and online settings.
  • Collect data and assist with preparing reports.
  • Collaborate with partners across BPL including the outreach team, branch library staff, and adult learning department to set up info sessions and tabling.
  • Maintain up-to-date stakeholder contact information and help identify new opportunities for community referrals.
  • Participate in relevant trainings and meetings.
  • Perform related duties and work on special projects as required.

  • High School degree required, BA preferred
  • 1-2 years relevant work experience preferred
  • Personal and firsthand experience with being a newcomer to New York City a plus.

Skills and Abilities

  • Excellent community outreach and engagement skills.
  • Strong interpersonal, oral, and written communication skills including the ability to present verbal information confidently to a range of audiences.
  • Excellent detail management and organizational skills.
  • Digitally literate and able to work and learn easily using technology.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with a team and on independent projects.
  • Successfully demonstrated customer service experience with the ability to work well with a diverse public.
  • Commitment to diversity and inclusion
  • Bi-lingual in English and Spanish, Chinese languages, Russian, Arabic, Kreyol, Wolof, French, or Ukrainian.
  • Required to work evenings and weekends as needed.

Flexibility and willingness to travel within the NYC Metro area.

This is a part-time position with a work schedule of up to 19 hours per week compensated at $25/hour

We seek professionals dedicated to providing excellent customer service, developing fruitful partnerships in the community, and implementing programs aligned with our mission and vision. title: Anatomic Pathology Product Specialist

In this high-impact role, you will serve as a trusted product, workflow, and laboratory operations expert, partnering closely with customers and sales teams to assess laboratory needs, identify opportunities for improvement, and position Agilent solutions that enhance operational efficiency, quality, productivity, and diagnostic confidence. You will support pre-sales activities, workflow assessments, evaluations, implementations, and post-installation success across clinical, research, and pharmaceutical/biopharmaceutical pathology laboratories.

We are seeking a consultative professional who understands pathology laboratory operations and can translate customer challenges into integrated solutions. Your technical expertise, workflow knowledge, and customer engagement skills will help laboratories improve performance and patient outcomes while strengthening Agilent's position as a leader in comprehensive pathology solutions.

  • Conduct comprehensive pathology workflow assessments to identify operational challenges, inefficiencies, and opportunities for improvement.

  • Partner with District Sales Managers, Account Managers, and cross-functional teams to advance complex solutions selling opportunities.

  • Deliver compelling product demonstrations, workflow analyses, and customer presentations tailored to laboratory and organizational needs.

  • Position Agilent's integrated anatomic pathology portfolio, including advanced staining platforms, digital pathology, informatics, and workflow optimization solutions.

  • Provide technical expertise and support during product evaluations, validation studies, implementations, and early adoption activities.

description:

title: Fund Development | Development and Events Associate
description:
The Development & Events Associate reports to the Senior Development Officer, Special Events & Donor Relations, and plays a key role in advancing Catholic Charities' fundraising, donor engagement, and stewardship efforts. This position works closely with Senior Leadership, the Board of Directors, Advisory Boards, donors, volunteers, corporate partners, and community stakeholders to support philanthropic initiatives that advance the agency's mission.

The Development & Events Associate is responsible for coordinating fundraising and donor recognition events, managing donor engagement activities and site visits, supporting donor stewardship initiatives, and cultivating relationships with corporate and community partners. The position serves as a vital member of the Development team by ensuring exceptional event execution, donor experiences, and administrative support that strengthen philanthropic investment and community engagement.

What you Deliver

Event Planning & Management

  • Coordinate and execute major fundraising events, including the annual Wine & Dine Gala and other agency fundraising initiatives.
  • Manage all aspects of event logistics, including sponsorship tracking, invitation preparation and distribution, guest management, registration systems, vendor coordination, volunteer engagement, and event-day operations.
  • Oversee donor recognition and stewardship events, including Caritas Mass & Brunch, Share the Mission Mass & Reception, Annual Meeting, and other special events as assigned.
  • Support regional fundraising and community engagement events throughout Galveston County, Fort Bend County, and surrounding service areas.
  • Maintain event calendars, project timelines, budgets, expense reports, and event documentation.
  • Research venues and vendors, negotiate services and pricing, obtain and review contracts, and ensure compliance with agency procurement requirements.
  • Coordinate event setup, load-in/load-out activities, inventory management, and post-event storage and organization.
  • Prepare event evaluations, donor reports, acknowledgments, invoices, and follow-up communications.

Donor Relations & Stewardship

  • Coordinate donor site visits and engagement opportunities, including scheduling, communications, preparation of donor materials, and coordination with program and facilities staff.
  • Serve as a primary liaison for Caritas Circle members, Board Directors, Advisory Board members, and key donor groups to support stewardship and engagement efforts.
  • Assist in the planning and execution of donor cultivation activities, tours, briefings, and recognition opportunities.
  • Provide personalized support to donors and volunteers to strengthen relationships and increase long-term engagement.
  • Maintain accurate donor, sponsorship, and event records within the organization's fundraising database and event management systems.

Corporate Partnerships & Fundraising Support

  • Conduct prospect research to identify potential corporate sponsors, community partners, and philanthropic opportunities.
  • Assist in cultivating local businesses and corporations to increase sponsorships, direct donations, in-kind support, volunteer engagement, and community partnerships.
  • Collaborate with the Development team to create sponsorship proposals, donor packets, fundraising collateral, and stewardship materials.
  • Support donor campaigns and special fundraising initiatives as assigned.

Communications & Collaboration

  • Partner with the Communications and Marketing team to develop and maintain event materials, sponsorship packets, donor communications, social media content, and fundraising webpages.
  • Ensure consistency and accuracy of donor-facing communications and event messaging.
  • Collaborate with agency leadership, program teams, operations staff, volunteers, and external partners to ensure successful donor and event experiences.
  • Support the Major Gifts Director, Senior Development Officer, and other Development leadership with research, reporting, and strategic initiatives.

Professional Development

  • Maintain knowledge of current fundraising trends, donor engagement strategies, philanthropy best practices, and nonprofit development standards.
  • Participate in professional development opportunities to strengthen fundraising, event management, and donor stewardship skills.
  • Perform other duties as assigned in support of the mission and goals of Catholic Charities.

title: Assembler I - 2nd Shift
description:
Every day, we get opportunities to make a positive impact – on our colleagues, partners, customers and society. Together, we’re pioneering the solutions of the future and unlocking the full potential of precious resources. Trusted to act on initiative, we challenge conventional thinking to develop world-leading technologies that inspire progress in vital areas, including energy, food, water and shipping.

As we push forward, the innovative, open spirit that fuels our 140-year-old start-up culture and rapid growth also drives our personal growth. So, as we shape a more resourceful, less wasteful world, we build our careers too.

As an Assembler I, this position works to assemble products by positioning and installing components and subassemblies according to drawings and instructions. Using a variety of hand and power tools, fixtures, work instructions and test equipment that are needed to perform a series of operations to correctly assemble coolers. Prepare work to be accomplished by studying assembly instructions, blueprint specifications, and parts lists; gathering parts, subassemblies, tools, and materials. Assemble components by examining connections for correct fit; fastening parts and subassemblies using hand and power tools. Verify specifications by measuring completed cooler components.   • Positions parts and subassemblies by reading blueprints and instructions.

  • Assembles components by examining connections for correct fit.

  • Demonstrated ability to read blueprints preferred.

  • Experience using industrial machines preferred.

  • Forklift operation certification preferred.

  • Overhead crane experience preferred

  • Demonstrates proficiency in one or more of the following equipment: radial drills, fin tube machinery, large vertical band saw, presses, breaks and shears.

Physical and Environmental Factors:

  • Regularly exert up to 50 lbs of force occasionally: 30 lbs of force frequently

  • Required to have visual acuity to operate motor vehicles and/or heavy equipment.

  • Lifting raw materials, assemblies, and equipment using lifts, or manually up to 50 lbs

  • An overhead crane will be used for items over 50lbs.

  • Work near hazards: moving machinery, vehicles, electrical currents, and chemicals

About the Role:

At Camunda, we are evolving how software gets built. We are looking for a Senior Product Builder to help shape the future of the Connectors Experience by combining product thinking, user empathy, UX judgment, and hands-on execution. This is a high-ownership role inside our Products organization for someone who can independently take a vague problem, define what success looks like, and turn it into a shipped outcome - working directly with customers and forward deployed engineers, and building in an AI-first environment. The role will start with a strong focus on the web app experience in Hub and Canvas (Web Modeler & Desktop Modeler), while also offering the opportunity over time to contribute across the stack where that enables faster end-to-end product delivery.

What You Will Do:

  • Discover and clarify meaningful user problems in the Connectors Experience by working closely with customers, forward deployed engineers, and internal stakeholders

  • Define success criteria and scope for features before build starts, rather than only executing a well-defined spec

  • Shape product direction through practical judgment, fast iteration, and a strong focus on solving the underlying problem rather than only implementing requests

  • Prototype, build, harden, ship, and iterate on product improvements across the Connectors Experience, owning complex features end-to-end

  • Use AI tools effectively to accelerate first drafts, implementation steps, iteration, and learning while maintaining a strong quality bar

  • Review AI-generated and peer output for maintainability, architectural fit, and UX quality, and share reusable patterns that raise the bar for other builders

  • Improve the speed, quality, and effectiveness of how the pod delivers product end-to-end

  • Ability to work fluidly across product thinking, user experience, and hands-on delivery

  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and turning open-ended problems into practical next steps

  • Strong collaboration and communication skills in a remote-first, pod-based environment, including helping others break down and sequence their work

  • Curiosity about users, fast learning loops, and a bias toward improving the product through iteration

Must Haves:

  • Hands-on experience independently building and shipping complex products in a software context, not only coordinating roadmap or requirements

  • Strong AI-native delivery habits: able to run AI-assisted workflows for complex features, diagnosing why AI output is weak and fixing the setup, not only the result

  • Ability to describe and shape intended user experience clearly across a full feature or surface area, including flow, hierarchy, states, copy, and accessibility expectations, catching pattern-level UX problems before they reach users

  • Strong product and customer judgment: able to turn vague direction into a clear product approach, define success criteria, cut scope intelligently, and know when evidence is strong enough to proceed

  • Sound technical judgment within an established architecture: reviews implementation quality beyond “does it work”, evaluates maintainability, test coverage, and architectural fit, and contributes beyond a pure frontend scope over time

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience with workflow software, orchestration, operations tooling, or similarly technical product surfaces

  • Experience working in small, high-autonomy pods with broad ownership across discovery, design, and delivery

  • Familiarity with connector building, connector marketplaces and technical partnerships

  • Track record independently planning and running validation, synthesizing findings into concrete product or UX changes, and helping improve team practices around lightweight product validation

  • Experience mentoring other builders or raising the quality bar beyond your immediate team

title: Supply Policy, Strategy and Transformation Consultant
description:
Our Deloitte Enterprise Performance team is at the forefront of enterprise technology, working across finance, supply chain, and IT operations to deliver holistic performance improvement and digital transformation. Join our team of strategic advisers and architects, differentiated by our industry depth to collaborate with leading solution providers and leverage your experience in strategy, process design, technology enablement, and operational services to enable heart-of-the-business solutions.

Work You'll Do

As a Project - Consultant of Strategy, Growth & Transformation on the Supply Chain & Network Operations team, you will be responsible for:
  • Supporting Supply Directorate operations by completing assigned tasks and processing supply policy requests
  • Providing technical input to support updates to defense supply policies, directives, and manuals
  • Conducting analysis and develop recommendations to improve supply chain processes, including asset visibility, cataloging, provisioning, demand planning, and munitions lifecycle management
  • Assisting with the drafting and maintenance of policies related to DMSMS, Defense Logistics Management Standards (DLMS), and Logistics Reassignments
  • Tracking and supporting reporting related to warehouse utilization, property accountability, LESO reporting, and Federal Catalog changes, including quarterly and annual reporting requirements
  • Supporting policy and process alignment across supply areas such as Class I (Subsistence), Class VIII (Medical Supplies & Equipment), demilitarization and disposition, warehousing, and cataloging/provisioning
  • Ensuring compliance with Federal Catalog standards and Defense Logistics Management Standards

A successful candidate would possess these skills:
  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The Team

Deloitte's Government & Public Services (GPS) practice - our people, ideas, technology and outcomes - is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Supply Chain & Network Operations offering advises, implements, and operates transformational solutions that bring world class supply network capabilities.

The Project Talent Model is designed for professionals with specialized skills that align to a current client need. Team members focus on delivering services to clients, without additional expectations related to business development or promotion. Their employment is tied to their role on a project, and they are eligible for a benefits package that is competitive for project delivery-focused professionals.

Qualifications

Required:
  • Bachelor's degree
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future
  • Active Secret security clearance required
  • 1+ years of experience with defense logistics or supply chain management policy concepts and practices
  • 1+ years of experience with workflow management or risk management in the defense industry
  • Ability to work on-site in Alexandria, VA up to 5 days/week (typical week 2-3 days on-site)

Preferred:
  • Experience supporting integrated program execution in a logistics or supply chain environment
  • Experience supporting reviews, assessments, and governance activities related to supply and materiel management
  • 1+ years of experience in policy analysis, policy development, and policy writing


For individuals assigned and/or hired to work in Virginia, Deloitte is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This compensation range is specific to Virginia and takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs. title: Lead Clinical Scientist
description:
A healthier future. It’s what drives us to innovate. To continuously advance science and ensure everyone has access to the healthcare they need today and for generations to come. Creating a world where we all have more time with the people we love. That’s what makes us Roche.

Genentech’s Research and Early Development (gRED) Early Clinical Development (ECD) organization is responsible for developing and executing early development clinical strategies and plans to provide proof-of-concept data with respect to safety, efficacy, and the utility of biomarkers for gRED new molecular entities. The Lead Clinical Scientist participates in development of clinical strategies for assigned molecule(s)/indication(s) and is responsible for developing and effective and efficient execution of the Clinical Development Plan (CDP) for one or more molecules. Lead Clinical Scientists are expected to perform their responsibilities independently, have core knowledge of the CS function to enable increased participation in department level initiatives, and may contribute to complex projects with supervision.

The Opportunity:

Your responsibilities in this role will include:

  • Contributes as a standing member of the Clinical Science Sub-Team.

  • Drives authoring, review and team decisions required to develop study protocols, ICFs, and study start-up documents documents requiring clinical expertise.

  • Conducts medical data review.

  • Processes and conducts regular review and analysis of protocol deviations.

  • Primary POC for protocol-related inquiries from internal colleagues and external sites.

  • May author, in collaboration with relevant team members and/or support functions, clinical sections of regulatory documents, or responses to healthy authority (HA) or ethics committee inquiries

  • Collaborates cross-functionally to develop simplified/novel/fit-for-purpose presentation of study data.

Who You Are:

  • Advanced clinical/science degree preferred (PharmD, PhD, MSN, MPH, etc.)

  • 4 or more years pharma/biotech industry experience preferred

  • Has experience working in complex matrixed setting(s)

  • Experience with cross-functional authoring full clinical trial protocols

  • In-depth understanding of drug development

  • Experience working with the principles and techniques of data analysis, interpretation, and assessment of clinical relevance

Relocation benefits are not available for this posting.

Onsite presence, on our South San Francisco campus, is expected for at least 3 days a week.

title: Contract Associate II - Remote

description:
Labcorp is a global leader in laboratory services, providing the insights and answers that help healthcare providers, patients, researchers, pharmaceutical companies and health systems make confident decisions and improve outcomes. Through our unparalleled science, data, technology and laboratory network, we advance diagnostics, accelerate innovation and help address some of the world’s most important health challenges. As we shape the future of healthcare, we are leveraging advanced technologies, intelligent digital solutions and data-driven innovation across our operations to enhance how work gets done and deliver greater value to customers and patients. With our global scale and deep expertise, you’ll have the opportunity to do meaningful work, grow your career and make a real impact on people’s health around the world. Together, we’re improving health and improving lives.


Labcorp is seeking a US remote based Contract Associate II to join our team to support our Mid-America division.

Work Schedule: Monday – Friday, 8am – 5pm central time zone

Job Responsibilities:

  • Provide end-to-end contracting of divisional client contracts, including drafting, reviewing, negotiating, and ensuring compliance with internal policies and legal requirements
  • Play a key part in supporting business objectives with urgency by facilitating timely contract execution, managing exceptions, and maintaining strong client relationships through clear and effective contract processes.

  • Review redlines using pre-approved language (approved deviations) and make determinations. Request escalations to Contract Associate III or management as needed.
  • Address client questions, and drafts emails and or participates on calls related to client questions
  • Escalate client concerns on information requests, compliance confirmations, pricing and business team questions, and requests for client calls as needed

  • Work closely with business units to understand client requirements, operational objectives, and service expectations to translate them into contractual terms
  • Advise internal stakeholders on contract structure, process, and risk considerations. Coordinate with stakeholders to identify and resolve contract exceptions and escalations
  • Create, update, and maintain client records within the contract management system, ensuring data accuracy and completeness.
  • Ensure accuracy, consistency, and completeness of client records in the contract management system
  • Monitor for duplicate, missing, or inconsistent client data and oversee resolution of discrepancies
  • Provide monitoring of unique/challenging client bid opportunities and communicates such opportunities to management for assignment
  • Assist in the preparation and submission of bid proposals in response to RFPs, RFQs, and other solicitation documents, including crafting responses to bid questions utilizing standard pre-approved language
  • Coordinate with cross-functional teams to gather necessary documentation, pricing, and compliance information

  • Package proposal for legal review and submission out to routine clients
  • Secure signatures, returns executed documents, and loads into contract management system

  • High school diploma or equivalent and 5 years or more of experience in contracts management OR Associate’s degree and 3 years or more of experience in contracts management

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2 years or more of experience in healthcare industry contracts management
  • Associate’s degree and 5 years or more of experience in contracts management

Additional Job Standards:

  • Strong communication skills; both written and verbal
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office Programs, Docusign and Adobe

  • Strong organization skills and able to adapt to high pressure
  • Able to change directions in workload based on required timeframes

title: Client Delivery Associate
description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Client Delivery Associate based in the United States.

This role supports the delivery of technology-enabled healthcare solutions by helping clients improve operational performance and reporting accuracy.
The Client Delivery Associate plays a key role in validating data, creating insights, and supporting client-facing initiatives.
Working across internal teams and client stakeholders, this position helps ensure smooth implementations and ongoing service excellence.
The role combines analytical skills, reporting expertise, organization, and a strong commitment to customer success.
The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, comfortable working with data, and motivated by solving complex business challenges.
This is an opportunity to contribute to meaningful healthcare improvements while developing expertise in revenue performance solutions and analytics.
Remote flexibility and exposure to cross-functional projects make this role a strong fit for proactive, collaborative professionals.

The Client Delivery Associate will support client delivery operations by managing reporting activities, validating data, assisting implementation projects, and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives. This role requires strong analytical capabilities, attention to detail, and the ability to collaborate effectively with internal teams and external stakeholders.

  • Create, analyze, and distribute recurring and ad hoc client reports, dashboards, and performance summaries.
  • Validate data accuracy and integrity by identifying inconsistencies, trends, errors, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support reporting enhancements, including data visualization and dashboard development using relevant analytics tools.
  • Maintain reporting schedules, operational documentation, and process tracking to ensure consistent delivery.
  • Assist with client implementations, account maintenance activities, and ongoing operational support.
  • Partner with internal teams to address reporting needs, resolve issues, and improve client outcomes.
  • Document trends, insights, and findings to support data-driven decision-making.
  • Contribute to team projects, process improvements, and initiatives designed to enhance service quality.
  • Provide organized administrative and operational support to ensure successful client delivery.
  • Communicate effectively with stakeholders while maintaining a strong client service mindset.

    • Requirements:

    The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented and analytical professional with experience supporting reporting, data validation, and client-focused operations. They should be comfortable managing multiple priorities, working with business data, and collaborating across teams in a healthcare or technology-driven environment.

    • Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent professional experience.
    • Minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in operations, analytics, reporting, client support, or a related field.
    • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data analysis, reporting, and spreadsheet management.
    • Experience creating reports, dashboards, or data visualizations; Power BI experience is a plus.
    • Strong attention to detail with the ability to identify data discrepancies and maintain accuracy.
    • Experience working with CRM tools, Microsoft Office applications, and reporting platforms.
    • Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage recurring deadlines and multiple priorities.
    • Strong written and verbal communication skills with a customer-focused approach.
    • Ability to analyze problems, identify solutions, and support process improvements.
    • Experience in healthcare operations, revenue cycle management, or technology-enabled services is a plus.

      • Benefits:

      • Eligibility to participate in an annual bonus plan with a target opportunity of 5%.
      • Comprehensive benefits package designed to support employee health and well-being.
      • Opportunities for continuous learning, professional development, and career growth.
      • Remote work flexibility.

U.S. Bank’s Fleet Product Group is seeking a strong ServiceNow Engineer / Developer to help modernize and improve the way we support Fleet customers. Fleet delivers products and solutions that help customers manage fuel and other business spending, and we are investing in better operational workflows, customer-facing support experiences, and integrated service management capabilities.

title: Major Gifts Officer
description:
The Position

Dream Centers is seeking a gifted, relational, and mission-driven leader to guide the Big Dream Early Learning capital campaign. This person will help carry a bold and beautiful vision for an emerging Dream Centers initiative designed to meet children and families at a critical moment with trauma-healing, relationship-centered early learning and support.

This is not simply a fundraising role. It is a vision-bearing role. The Major Gifts Officer will manage the campaign strategy, coordinate existing campaign committees and subcommittees, cultivate major donors, and help invite the Colorado Springs philanthropic community into the dream.

The right person for this role will know how to tell the story, build trust, follow through with excellence, and help donors see that their generosity can change the trajectory of a child’s life and strengthen a family’s ability to carry forward with stability, skill, and connection.

The ideal candidate will be deeply connected in the Colorado Springs philanthropic community and will bring established relationships, credibility, and trust with local donors, foundations, business leaders, churches, civic partners, and community champions.

Responsibilities

Campaign Leadership and Strategy

  • As part of the Dream Center’s Executive Leadership team, lead the planning, coordination, execution, and management of the Big Dream Early Learning capital campaign.
  • Develop and maintain a comprehensive campaign plan, including goals, timelines, donor segments, cultivation strategies, solicitation plans, stewardship practices, and committee engagement rhythms.
  • Work closely with Dream Centers leadership to clarify campaign priorities, funding needs, messaging, and donor engagement opportunities.
  • Track campaign progress against goals and provide regular updates to executive leadership, the board, campaign committees and subcommittees, and other key stakeholders.
  • Identify potential risks, gaps, or opportunities in the campaign and recommend adjustments as needed.

Steering Committee and Subcommittee Management

  • Manage and support the existing campaign committees and subcommittees.
  • Ensure committee members are clear on goals, roles, timelines, assignments, and next steps.
  • Coordinate committee meetings, agendas, materials, follow-up items, donor assignments, and accountability rhythms.
  • Help keep campaign leaders engaged, informed, encouraged, and moving together toward shared goals.
  • Serve as a central point of coordination between Dream Centers staff, committee members, subcommittee chairs, and organizational leadership.
  • Create a culture of momentum, clarity, ownership, and relational trust across the campaign structure.

Colorado Springs Philanthropic Engagement

  • Bring deep knowledge of and connection to the Colorado Springs philanthropic community.
  • Identify, cultivate, and engage local donors, foundations, businesses, churches, civic leaders, and community partners who may be aligned with the vision of Big Dream Early Learning.
  • Open doors, build bridges, and strengthen relationships between Dream Centers and key philanthropic networks in the region.
  • Represent Dream Centers with warmth, credibility, professionalism, and deep alignment with the mission.
  • Understand the local giving landscape and help shape strategies that are relationally wise, community-centered, and effective.

Major Donor Cultivation and Solicitation

  • Build and manage a portfolio of major gift prospects, including individuals, families, foundations, churches, businesses, and community partners.
  • Create personalized cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship strategies for key donors.
  • Prepare donor briefings, proposals, campaign materials, pledge requests, and follow-up communications.
  • Support the CEO, executive leadership, board members, committee members, and subcommittee leaders in donor meetings and asks.
  • Ensure every donor interaction is thoughtful, timely, relational, and aligned with the heart of Dream Centers.

Storytelling and Campaign Communication

  • Tell the story of Big Dream Early Learning in a way that connects the innovative science of this groundbreaking program with the lived experience and currently unmet needs of children and families.
  • Translate complex needs into simple, compelling opportunities for generosity.
  • Protect the dignity of children and families in all storytelling.

Donor Stewardship and Campaign Operations

  • Develop and manage a strong stewardship plan for campaign donors, including gift acknowledgments, impact updates, recognition opportunities, and personal follow-up.
  • Maintain accurate donor records, contact reports, pledge documentation, committee assignments, and campaign tracking systems.
  • Coordinate with finance and operations teams to ensure gifts, pledges, restrictions, and reports are handled with excellence.
  • Prepare regular campaign dashboards and progress reports.
  • Ensure campaign activity is organized, confidential, and donor-centered.

title: WFM Capacity & Analytics Planner
description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy.

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

Gusto is looking for a senior, technically minded workforce management planner who can design and scale AI-powered forecasting and capacity planning systems. You will report into the Planning People Empower and play a leading role in shaping how AI is adopted across forecasting, scheduling, and intraday operations. This role is equal parts strategic design and hands-on execution: you'll build the frameworks, pipelines, and governance structures that elevate WFM from reactive to predictive.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

  • Use AI to identify demand shifts, seasonal patterns, and emerging workforce risks before they impact operations.
  • Connect AI-generated insights to operational decisions across staffing, scheduling, and capacity planning.
  • Develop and maintain capacity plans, providing recommendations on hiring, staffing, and efficiency improvements for our CX teams.
  • Participate in an on-call PagerDuty rotation to monitor and respond to real-time alerts — including system outages, service level breaches, and routing failures — ensuring rapid escalation and resolution during off-hours incidents.
  • Design scalable AI-enabled WFM workflows across forecasting, scheduling, and intraday functions.
  • Build and maintain AI-powered WFM data pipelines that integrate multiple data sources (volume, AHT, shrinkage) to enable predictive and near-real-time insights.
  • Continuously monitor and adjust forecasts using AI-driven models and traditional methods as demand evolves.
  • Design governance frameworks for AI-enabled WFM workflows, including monitoring, validation, and escalation processes.
  • Partner with Legal, Data, and Product to ensure AI implementations meet organizational standards and compliance requirements.
  • Lead cross-functional AI initiatives for WFM, influencing how teams across the organization use AI in planning and operations.
  • Facilitate stakeholder meetings on forecasting, capacity planning, and AI adoption progress as member and facilitator aligned to the Operational Rhythm Meeting structure.
  • Identify potential risks to workforce capacity and proactively devise contingency plans.
  • Collaborate with stakeholders to implement risk mitigation strategies.
  • Evaluate and recommend process enhancements to boost efficiency and capacity utilization.
  • Analyze data to identify gaps and opportunities within the CX organization.

Here’s what we're looking for:

  • AI fluency required: Demonstrated ability to adopt and operationalize AI tools in a WFM or contact center context; designing or implementing AI/ML-powered forecasting, automation, or analytics workflows. Gusto is an AI-forward company and active AI use is expected daily.
  • Strong analytical and data visualization skills; demonstrated experience building dashboards and interactive reporting tools to surface WFM insights for operations and leadership; demonstrated analytical skills in volume forecasting, employee workloads, and staffing optimization.
  • Excellent judgment, communication, and problem-solving skills — able to translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations for stakeholders at all levels.
  • Familiarity with COPC, ICMI, and/or SWPP standards is a plus.
  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
  • 7+ years in a capacity planning and forecasting role
  • Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence planning and operations practices across teams
  • Experience building or managing data pipelines that integrate multiple WFM data sources (volume, AHT, shrinkage, scheduling)
  • Proficiency in data modeling, statistical analysis, and data visualization
  • Experience in a high-volume, fast-paced contact center environment
  • Experience with BPOs
  • Familiarity with AI governance concepts including model monitoring, validation, and responsible AI practices

The cash compensation range for thisrole is $105,000/yearly to $129,00/yearly in Denver and Las Vegas, and most remote locations, and $98,775/yearly to $121,000/yearly in Phoenix. Remote locations will vary based on our geographical pay approach. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate location, experience and expertise, and may vary from the level and amounts listed above.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. This department works cross-functionally with operations, production, marketing, and venue partners to help ensure events meet organizational standards and deliver a high-quality fan experience. By supporting market research, promotional planning, and event execution, the team plays a key role in driving attendance and overall event success. Their work directly supports the UFC’s live event strategy and business growth.

Responsibilities

  • Assist with organizing, formatting, and maintaining event schedules.
  • Conduct research on competitive events and live entertainment markets in cities where UFC events are held.
  • Assist with preparation for meetings with current and prospective on-sale marketing and area partners.
  • Support the creation and organization of presentation materials for internal and external meetings.
  • Assist with activating Street Team initiatives and in-market promotional efforts.

Qualifications

Program Details

We offer internship opportunities across IMG, On Location, Professional Bull Riders (PBR), TKO Corporate, UFC, and WWE. Locations include New York City, Atlanta, Austin, Raleigh, Dallas, Fort Worth, Las Vegas, and Stamford, CT. All internships are in the office and in-person, unless otherwise noted.

In addition to hands-on experience and exposure to the global sports and entertainment industry, interns participate in events such as welcome/farewell sessions, a speaker series featuring company leaders, and career training workshops addressing everything from LinkedIn profile enhancement to resume building, interviewing skills, and networking.

Internships are 40 hours per week, Monday through Friday, or standard local working hours in the intern location.

Recruitment Process

Our process consists of four steps.

  • 1. Tell us your story. In addition to your application and resume, please attach a word document and in 300 words max, share why you’re interested in the role. What are the unique perspectives, abilities, and qualities you would bring to the role? What do you hope to learn?

Our program is designed for rising juniors, rising seniors, and those within six months of graduation from an undergraduate university, unless otherwise noted.

title: Director of Trauma
description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talent team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels included, respected, empowered and recognised.


What You Can Expect

Paragon 28, a trailblazing Zimmer Biomet company, is looking for a visionary Director of Trauma to revolutionize our global footprint.

Take the helm of a high-growth portfolio and define the future of trauma and limb salvage surgery. In this powerhouse leadership role, you will architect the global commercial strategy, drive product lifecycle management, and spearhead high-impact product launches across both domestic and international markets. You will build an integrated, world-class procedural ecosystem that spans fixation, external fixation, biologics, and enabling technologies to optimize surgical workflows. By cultivating deep partnerships with elite surgeons and collaborating cross-functionally with R&D, Clinical Affairs, and Sales, you will turn disruptive innovation into widespread clinical adoption. If you are a strategic market-builder ready to lead a dedicated team and transform patient care on a global scale, we want you.

How You'll Create Impact

Executive Leadership & Strategy

  • Drive Strategy: Own global Trauma commercial strategy and annual marketing plans to hit revenue goals.
  • Lead Commercialization: Head global launch planning, product positioning, and economic messaging for new introductions.
  • Define Market Entry: Determine launch strategies via internal development, acquisitions, licensing, or supply partnerships.
  • Analyze Performance: Evaluate marketing campaign ROI, tracking costs against revenue results to optimize spend.

Field Enablement & Sales Partnership

  • Accelerate Growth: Partner with Sales Leadership to boost surgeon conversion, market penetration, and account expansion.
  • Support Value Analysis: Create economic messaging and procedural efficiency strategies to win hospital system approvals.
  • Educate Markets: Lead surgeon awareness and patient education initiatives with commercial and compliance teams.


Portfolio Innovation & KOL Engagement

  • Build KOL Networks: Develop strategic surgeon partnerships to drive innovation, clinical education, and market expansion.
  • Shape the Pipeline: Collaborate with design surgeons and R&D to spot unmet needs and spark future innovation.
  • Track Industry Trends: Monitor medical literature, competitor moves, and conferences to stay ahead of scientific advancements.

Curriculum Development & Medical Education

  • Own Training Curriculum: Lead the creation, delivery, and maintenance of all internal and external training programs.
  • Modernize Content: Design multi-media educational learning objects, electronic tools, and complex instructional handouts.
  • Optimize Programs: Continuous improvement of course agendas, lesson plans, and demonstrations alongside subject matter experts.
  • Execute Educational Events: Partner with Events teams to run workshops, CME courses, labs, and regional surgeon programs.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Compliance

  • Unify Teams: Act as the central commercial bridge across Sales, R&D, Clinical, Regulatory, Operations, and Supply Chain.
  • Ensure Total Compliance: Align all educational activities and materials with federal, state, and AdvaMed codes of conduct.

Your Background

Graduate degree preferred.

· BA or BS; will consider equivalent combination of education and experience

· Demonstrated ability to develop and teach educational curriculum.

· Experience in orthopedics, preferably within trauma, foot & ankle, deformity correction, or medical education.

· Ability to support large-scale surgeon education programs, labs, and national commercial initiatives.

· Must demonstrate strong communication and presentation skills.

· Must be able to manage multiple, detailed projects, prioritize urgent needs simultaneously, and work cross functionally.

· Must be able to operate independently with little direction Ability to engage in high level scientific and engineering conversations with surgeon audiences (domestic and international).

· Excellent planning, organizational and analytical skills.

· Strong collaboration skills and willingness to be a team player.

· Ability and willingness to travel frequently as required.

· High paced growth environment-need to be comfortable managing many different related roles within the organization.

· Proficient in MS Office Suite (Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook

Travel Expectations

Position requires approximately 30% overnight travel throughout the country.

Compensation Data

Salary Range: $170,000 - $210,000 USD Annually depending on skills and experience

title: Enterprise Solutions Engineer - Nordics
description:

As an Enterprise Solutions Engineer, you will serve as a trusted technical partner for enterprise customers and prospects, helping them design and implement modern observability solutions. You will bridge customer needs with technical capabilities by supporting discovery, architecture design, demonstrations, and proof-of-concept initiatives. Working closely with sales, product, and engineering teams, you will help organizations unlock the value of cloud-native technologies while improving reliability and performance. This role offers the opportunity to influence product direction, solve complex technical challenges, and work with innovative technologies such as OpenTelemetry, Kubernetes, and distributed systems. You will join a fast-moving environment where your expertise and ideas can have a direct impact on customer success and product evolution.

description:
Foods you love. Brands you trust. And a career that empowers you to grow.

At Nestlé USA, we’re all working towards the same goal – to delight and deliver for our consumers. With a rich portfolio of beloved brands, including DiGiorno, Toll House, and Coffee mate, in 97% of U.S. households, we have a unique opportunity – and responsibility – to be there for every moment in our consumers’ lives.

Joining Nestlé means becoming part of an inclusive workplace that inspires innovation, encourages strategic thinking and creativity, and celebrates your achievements. No matter where you work within the organization, you are empowered to challenge the status quo, embrace risk-taking, and pioneer new ideas. Our supportive and collaborative environment encourages bold ambitions and continuous learning so that everyone can grow and thrive.

This position is not eligible for Visa Sponsorship.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Senior Customer Account Specialist (SCAS) is responsible for managing, developing, and driving category growth across key indirect customers in an assigned territory. This role focuses on achieving annual sales and commercial spend targets, building strong customer relationships, and executing category and customer business plans. The position requires close collaboration with Wholesaler Customer Account Teams, Commercial Development, Sales Analyst, Shopper Marketing, Category Management, and Field Execution Teams to deliver exceptional results and drive market share gains.

  • Organization: Neighborhood Grocers Team (NGT is a dedicated Sales Team within Nestlé USA that drives growth by partnering with a diverse network of neighborhood retailers and wholesalers across all NUSA Divisions)
  • Team: West Sr. Customer Account Specialist Team
  • Customers: Crest Foods, Reasor’s, Homeland, & Pruett’s. Retailers subject to change.
  • Division/Category Responsibilities: Wall-to-Wall
  • Location/Travel Requirements: This position is open to being REMOTE, preferred location in Oklahoma City, OK. However, if candidate is located close to the Solon or Rogers Office, the hybrid workplace guidelines apply and 3 days in office would be required.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Category Strategy: Product / Brand Objectives

  • Drive category growth (category-first mindset) and achieve/exceed annual sales and commercial spend targets.
  • Maintain and manage profitable growth to drive market share gains.
  • Collaborate with Wholesaler CAM (s) to develop customer promotion plans for Indirect Retailers based on distribution, category trends, and promotional activities.
  • Partner with Category Management and Sales Analysts to transform 4Ps analytics and insights into action.

Customer Strategy: Sales Performance Targets and Customer Relations

  • Develop and present business plans, new item presentations, distribution optimization, and customer promotional calendars.
  • Manage day-to-day responsibilities for assigned customers.
  • Build and maintain strong business relationships internally with cross-functional partners & teammates as well as externally with customer personnel.

Win at Retail: Improving Execution

  • Drive excellence in execution through continual interaction with Nestlé Retail Sales (NRS) team and/or Distributor Sales team.

Right People, Right Place: Talent Development

  • Own personal development through adoption of capability tools and participation in career development programs.
  • Drive category growth and meet/exceed high performance targets.
  • Develop critical behaviors (Ways of Winning) through robust PDP process.

Develop Valued Capabilities

  • Utilize data and reporting tools to support 4P (Product, Price, Place, Promotion) objectives and provide actionable insights.
  • Most SCAS roles are ‘wall to wall’ responsibilities – all NUSA divisions and categories

Integrated Approach: Team & Cross-Functional Communication

  • Partner with CAM on forecast, trade, and events.
  • Actively ensure timely & effective communication with internal partners – Leaders, CAMs, Commercial Development, Account Associate, Sales Analyst, Field Execution Teams (Nestlé Retail Sales & Distributor Team), Finance (RGM & TFS), etc… (Business Support Center – BSC, as applicable)

REQUIRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree required (business-related preferred), and minimum of 2 years of relevant sales experience is required.
  • Analyst and customer-facing project experience preferred (an ideal candidate is someone with at least two of three roles - an NRS role, an Analyst role, an Associate role and have experience with some level of customer interaction to showcase strong analytical, communication and interpersonal skills).
  • Strong ability for collaboration, courage, speed, and agility; being a productive team player.
  • Effective communication skills, both oral and written, strong judgement in decision making, good problem-solving skills, thinks strategically, and a customer service orientation.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Teams, Outlook, Excel, and PowerPoint) and ability to work in various operating systems (i.e., customer portals).
  • Strategic analytical skills; experience with data sources and such as Power BI, Circana, & Nielsen
  • Skilled in business mathematics.
  • Exceptional organizational and time management skills are essential.
  • Strong presentation and negotiation skills.
  • Knowledge of sales fundamentals: pricing, promotion, assortment, merchandising, and financial reconciliation.
  • Ability to create compelling, fact-based selling stories and customer plans.
  • Ability to resolve issues promptly and communicate potential impacts to stakeholders.

title: Lead Analyst - Product Analytics
description:
Who is Quantium?

Quantium is a world leader in data science and artificial intelligence. Established in Australia in 2002, Quantium is a global team of more than 1,200 people across 14 locations with a unique blend of capabilities across product and consulting services to help businesses unlock value from data and analytics. Quantium partners with the world's largest corporations to forge a better, more intelligent world.

As a Senior Analyst in our Product Analytics team, you'll be an experienced technical contributor taking on increased responsibility in designing and delivering sophisticated analytics solutions. Working within cross-functional teams, you'll apply advanced data science techniques and collaborate with engineers, product specialists, and analysts across our global teams.

This role offers the opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while exploring leadership responsibilities, contributing to team capability development, and growing your influence within our analytics community.

How You'll Create Impact

  • Design and build sophisticated analytics solutions with growing independence, supporting Analytics Leads with solution architecture and technical decision-making
  • Develop analytics approaches that can be scaled and reused across different business contexts
  • Create detailed specifications for analytics work that engineering teams can implement
  • Take responsibility for significant components of analytics solutions including models, algorithms, and optimisation approaches
  • Work with complex datasets using cloud platforms and modern data engineering tools
  • Apply advanced data science methods with attention to quality and scalability
  • Use AI tools effectively to enhance analytical workflows and support team productivity
  • Support product roadmap delivery and ongoing operational requirements
  • Contribute to technical discussions about approach, effort estimates, and timelines

The Superpowers You'll Be Bringing To The Team

Technical depth: Strong proficiency in Python and SQL, with solid cloud platform experience (GCP, AWS, or Azure) and a good grasp of data science methods — from experimental design and feature engineering through to model development and machine learning.

Problem-solving: You approach complex analytical challenges methodically, working both independently and collaboratively to find scalable, high-quality solutions.

Communication: You communicate clearly across diverse, globally distributed teams, and enjoy sharing knowledge and supporting the capability development of those around you.

Growth mindset: You're ready to take on more — whether that's project coordination, mentoring junior analysts, or driving process improvements across the team.

Required Experience And Capabilities

  • Degree in engineering, mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics, or a related quantitative field — or equivalent demonstrated analytical capability
  • 4–7 years of experience in data science, analytics, or similar technical roles, ready for increased responsibility
  • Strong proficiency in Python and SQL with experience handling complex data challenges
  • Good experience with a major cloud platform — Google Cloud Platform (GCP), AWS, or Azure — and cloud-based data processing
  • Solid understanding of data science methods including experimental design, feature engineering, and model development
  • Growing expertise in machine learning algorithms, statistical modelling, and their practical application
  • Familiarity with software engineering practices including version control, testing, and documentation
  • Strong problem-solving approach with the ability to work both independently and collaboratively
  • Good communication skills for working with diverse teams across different time zones
  • Interest in supporting team members and willingness to take on coordination and leadership responsibilities

Desirable

  • Experience with generative AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot) or enthusiasm for learning
  • Retail analytics background including consumer behaviour, promotional analysis, or transaction data

What Could Your Quantium Experience Look Like?

Working at Quantium will allow you to challenge your imagination. You will get to solve complex problems using rigour, precision and by asking great questions — but it also means you can think big, outside the box and push your problem-solving skills to the max.

By joining the Quantium team, you'll get to:

Forge your path: So many of our team have moved around different teams or offices. You'll be in the driver's seat, and we empower you to make your career your own.

Find your kind: Embrace diversity and connect with your tribe (think foodies, dog lovers, readers, or runners).

Make an impact: Leave your mark. Your contributions resonate, regardless of your role or rank.

Benefits

On top of the Quantium Experience, you will enjoy a range of great benefits that go beyond the ordinary. Some of these include:

Flexible work arrangements: Achieve work-life balance at your own pace with hybrid and flexible work arrangements.

Global mobility: As we expand globally, there are lots of exciting opportunities to work abroad with Quantium.

Remote working: Embrace the opportunity to work outside of your assigned home location for up to 2 months every year.

Apply now and let's forge a better, more intelligent world together!

title: Cloud Security Engineer (Secret Clearance)
location: Washington, District of Columbia, United States
description:
Cloud environments continue to transform how organizations operate, and securing those environments requires professionals who can design, implement, and strengthen controls across complex platforms. As a Cloud Security Engineer, you will help assess and enhance security across Amazon Web Services (AWS), Google Cloud Platform (GCP), and Microsoft Azure environments. This role supports cloud security architecture, engineering, monitoring, and risk reduction activities to help organizations protect critical systems and data. You will work with cross-functional teams to identify gaps, implement controls, and support secure cloud adoption..

Work You'll Do

As a Cloud Security Engineer on the Cloud Security team, you will be responsible for...
  • Assess cloud environments across AWS, GCP, and Azure to identify security risks, control gaps, and configuration issues.
  • Design, implement, and improve cloud security controls, including identity and access management, network security, encryption, logging, and monitoring.
  • Support cloud security architecture reviews for new and existing solutions and provide recommendations aligned to security and compliance requirements.
  • Investigate cloud security events and findings, analyze root causes, and support remediation activities with engineering and operations teams.
  • Develop and maintain technical documentation, standards, baselines, and reports related to cloud security controls and cloud risk management.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:
